comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
**κ* per arm and group (answers this request).** Grid κ ∈ {0.25 … 64}, each pool's own smallest κ with group-mean coverage ≥ 0.90; width as a multiple of the oracle width (z·SE + |bias|); C2 is HC0 inflated to the same mean width. Tables: `results/p6/p6_true_m_{confirmatory,original}.csv` on `paper-repo` `dev` (7fa63e8), rows with `kappa_rule` "smallest grid kappa…" or "pooled coverage 0.90 not reached…", `pool` = the group.

**Block (confirmatory), κ\* / coverage / width ÷ oracle / C2 coverage:**

| pool | cubic | true M (whole [0,1]) | noise-free cubic | lean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| all but (d), 585 cells | 0.25 / 0.989 / 8.7 / 1.000 | not reached: 0.846 at κ=64 (69×) | 2 / 0.907 / 4.9 / 1.000 | not reached: 0.857 (70×) |
| smooth, finite M, 423 | 0.25 / 0.998 / 9.6 / 1.000 | 0.25 / 0.913 / 1.04 / 0.900 | 0.5 / 0.919 / 1.21 / 0.941 | not reached: 0.877 (31×) |
| (b)+(e), 162 | 0.25 / 0.966 / 6.7 / 1.000 | not reached: 0.591 (0.61×); C2 0.591 | 16 / 0.950 / 70 / 1.000 | not reached: 0.805 (155×) |

**Original cells (exploratory):**

| pool | cubic | true M | noise-free cubic | lean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| all but (d), 1080 | 0.25 / 0.978 / 11.5 | not reached: 0.771 | 8 / 0.916 / 14.3 | not reached: 0.851 |
| smooth, finite M, 648 | 0.25 / 0.997 / 12.4 | not reached: 0.895 at κ=64 (71×) | not reached: 0.895 (42×) | not reached: 0.874 (23×) |
| (b)+(e), 432 | 0.25 / 0.948 / 10.3 | not reached: 0.585 (0.63×) | 4 / 0.901 / 12.5 | not reached: 0.817 |

- **(b)/(e), as predicted:** M = 0 gives plain HC0, and coverage stays at 0.59 whatever κ is. The cubic M̂ covers them (0.966) only at 6.7 times the oracle width, because its M̂ is noise.
- **Smooth pool:** the true M reaches 0.90 within 1.5 times the oracle width on the block only. On the original cells it never reaches 0.90 (0.895 at κ=1 and beyond); the remaining miss is cell-level and does not shrink with κ.
- **Lean** does not reach 0.90 in any pool.
- **Same cells, no change to κ̂ or the verdicts;** exploratory.

issue.author: paper-repo
issue.body:
From `paper-repo`: your corrections on #4 are applied on `dev` (47da74a), together with the review of version 1 (paper-repo#12). Please confirm, against the code, what the text now says each result is:

1. **Variance** (Results, "Variance"; abstract; Appendix Fig A2B): the slopes -0.50 (n), +0.55 [0.547, 0.556] (1+d), -0.50 (p(1-p)) are on **log SD** of the Chin regression over **42 cells of the plain SBM, Bernoulli, sigma = 0.5: the null column and mechanism (a) at s = 1/2** (`c1_exponents`); the L exponents (n^-0.02, (1+d)^1.09, [p(1-p)]^-0.99) are over 210 graph draws.
2. **Absolute R2 of log |bias|** (Results, "gains must be read next to"): on the 1224 cells with an exact prediction, S-bar -0.22, S_adj -0.06, corner x curvature -0.12, p(1-p) -0.26 (`bias_reference.csv`), exact prediction 0.987. I no longer say "above a constant": there is no constant row for log |bias| in the tables, so the text says "negative absolute held-out R2". Is that right? The appendix says "2178 cells" for the log RMSE R2s.
3. **Definitions in Design** (new): a *cell* = one combination of graph, degree, assignment design, p, mechanism, spillover share, noise level; *ties* = cells outside D; D* = the part of D in which misfit of the specification supplies at least 20% of the variance of the estimate (`sel_share` >= 0.2, chosen on the other half of the draws). Please correct any of these.
4. **Appendix**: Dependence on p (seven panels; RMSE minimiser 0.40 for (c) and 0.60 for (g) at d = 20); Grid (R6 for Stanford3 / ego-Facebook as you wrote; the extension list); a new paragraph "Fitted-form oracle" with Fig A9 (the numbers from `or_fit_check.csv`: shares at a grid end 5/59/86% for (c), 59/82/86% for (e); RMSE fitted vs known 0.087/0.087, 0.549/0.233, 2.00/0.541 for (c); spread 0.05% at d = 20 for (c)); Discussion: (e) bias prediction outside the interval in 10% of its cells.
5. **Coverage by family** (Results, "Confidence intervals"): Stanford3 0.52, ego-Facebook 0.66, Watts-Strogatz 0.82 on the 1800 `figure` cells: please confirm against `c8_coverage_by_family.csv`.

One question for your decision. The review of version 1 (M6) says that cluster Horvitz-Thompson and a graph-neural-network estimator, which the paper lists as not run, must be run or shown infeasible before the final version. The starter literature lists both families. A cluster HT estimator on the cluster-design cells and a small GNN (own treatment plus neighbours' treatments as input, prediction at the two corners, graph-cluster cross-validation) on the Tier A sample of cells look feasible on CPU at n = 3000. If you can run them, deliver the cells with their intervals; if you judge them infeasible within the budget, say why in one line and the paper will say so. I will place whatever is delivered.

comments.body:
Checked against the code and tables.

1. **Variance.** Correct as you state it. `c1_exponents` (`analysis/claims.py::c1_exponents`) regresses log SD of the Chin estimate on log n, log(1+d), log p(1−p) over 42 cells of the plain SBM (core and n-slice runs), Bernoulli, the null column and mechanism (a) at s = ½; σ = 0.5 slopes −0.504, +0.551 [0.547, 0.556], −0.504. The L exponents (−0.019, 1.093, −0.995) are `c1_L_exponents.csv`, 210 graph draws (21 runs).
2. **Absolute R² of log|bias|.** Your numbers match `bias_reference.csv` on 1224 cells. "Negative absolute held-out R²" is correct as worded. There is no constant row yet; I added one (`constant (held-out training mean)`, same folds and cells; commit ac99db2), the job is running, and I will say here when the file is delivered. A constant's held-out R² is slightly below 0 by construction (the held-out mean differs from the pooled mean), so the text can then say whether S̄ etc. are below a constant. The appendix's 2178 for the R² of log RMSE is right (`diagnostic_absolute.csv`).
3. **Definitions.** Cell: right (run = graph family, n, degree, design, p, base; × mechanism × spillover share s × noise level). D* = D ∩ {`sel_share` ≥ 0.2}; `sel_share` = graph-draw mean of the misfit variance over the total variance of the estimate, computed on one half of the assignments, and the part-(i) test uses the other half (`make_diag.py`, D, D*, "D minus D*"). Ties = cells outside D. Correct.
4. **Appendix.** All matches `or_fit_check.csv` (grid-end shares 4.8/59/86% for (c) and 59/82/86% for (e); RMSE 0.087/0.087, 0.549/0.233, 2.00/0.541; relative SSE spread 0.055% at d = 20 for (c)). (e) outside the interval in 9.8% of its cells with finite-n centring (`c2_prediction_check`), so "10%" is right. RMSE minimiser (c) 0.40, (g) 0.60 at d = 20: right.
5. **Coverage by family: one correction on provenance.** 0.52 / 0.66 / 0.82 are right for the 1800 figure cells (Stanford3 0.522, ego-Facebook 0.663, WS 0.817; all families: BA 0.744, DCSBM 0.754, ER 0.800, SBM 0.757), but `c8_coverage_by_family.csv` is a different population (s = 0.5 only, all non-null cells; Stanford3 0.465, ego-Facebook 0.659, WS 0.829). I added `claims/c8_coverage_figure_by_family.csv` for the 1800 cells (it comes with the next export); until then quote the family numbers as "on the 1800 cells" and do not cite `c8_coverage_by_family`.

**Baselines (your question).** Both are feasible and both are running now.
- *GNN*: 2-layer mean-aggregation GNN on (own treatment, mean neighbour treatment, log degree), weight decay and epoch chosen by graph-cluster hold-out + corner loss as for the other Tier A learners, prediction at the two corners. The 14 Tier A cells, same assignments as the other estimators (bit-identity of the stream checked on the Chin estimate), 50 draws per cell instead of 200 (cost; stated in the deliverable), null column and six mechanisms at s = 0.5. Jobs are queued on a loaded host.
- *Cluster Horvitz–Thompson*: the exposure-based Hajek estimators of the grid (q = 0.75 and 1.0, with the exposure probabilities of the cluster-randomisation design, Monte Carlo) are already run on all cluster-design cells; that is the Ugander–Karrer–Backstrom–Kleinberg estimator in its self-normalised (Hajek) form, and the text should not call cluster HT "not run" but "run in its Hajek form". I am adding the unnormalised HT form (ht75, ht100) by rerunning the 22 cluster runs with the same assignments; I will deliver both and say here when they are in.
I will deliver the GNN and HT cells as soon as the jobs end, together with the block results.

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
From `experiment-repo`: both items are delivered on `paper-repo` `dev` (a0812a0): `results/populations.csv` and `results/parity_d.csv` (with `.meta.json`), computed by `analysis/populations.py` and `analysis/parity_d.py`. Your reading of the populations is right except where noted; every count below was recomputed from the exported tables and reproduces.

**1. Populations** (all at noise multiple 0.5 unless stated; "a–f" are the six planned mechanisms; (g) is the convex mirror)
- **2193** (Table 1, per noise level; 126 runs): s ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75}, mechanisms a–f, Bernoulli *and* cluster designs, every run except the fine-s and p-grid runs. It includes the edge-noise, no-baseline sanity and convex-mirror (c) runs.
- **1797** (Bernoulli rows of Table 1; 104 runs): the same, Bernoulli only. 2193 − 1797 = the 396 cluster-design cells.
- **2178** (diagnostic cells; 121 runs; Fig. 5 and the absolute R² of log RMSE): s > 0, a–f, both designs (1782 Bernoulli + 396 cluster), edge-noise and sanity runs included. It excludes the 15 convex-mirror cells that Table 1 keeps (hence 2193 − 15).
- **1800** (Fig. 4; 94 runs): Bernoulli, true feature graph (no edge noise), a–f, s > 0, fine-s runs included; no sanity, convex-mirror or p-grid runs. It is a subset of 1797 (the 108 edge-noise, 36 sanity and 15 convex cells are out, the 162 fine-s cells in).
- **1974** (oracle rule; 107 runs): *every* Bernoulli cell with s > 0, mechanisms a–g, except the p-grid runs. It therefore includes edge-noise, sanity and the convex mirror, including the 15 cells of (g), so "a–f" is wrong for it.
- **1440** (ŝ rule; 80 runs): the cells of the 1974 that have an estimated share in the exported table, 240 per mechanism a–f. 36 of them are edge-noise or sanity cells (18 each), a storage artefact. Dropping them changes the rule from 91.8% to 91.95% right on the remaining 1404, and the base rate from 80.2% to 80.3%.
- **1224** (exact bias prediction; 68 runs): non-null cells a–f at s ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75} that have the exact population-OLS prediction: 204 per mechanism; families, real graphs, core, size and sanity runs. There is none for cluster, edge-noise, community-baseline or fine-s cells.
- **9795** (Fig. A2A; 107 runs): every Bernoulli cell with a mechanism a–f at all five noise multiples (0.25–4) in the Tier G regression, p-grid runs excluded. It is 1959 cells × 5 noise multiples and includes the fine-s grid (s = 0.1…0.9).

**2. Learner parity on (d)** (`parity_d.csv`, 10000 resamples; the median is the median of per-cell ratios of RMSE to the regression, as in the tier summary):

| learner | median ratio | 95% interval (cells) | 95% interval (runs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| boosting | 0.99 | [0.70, 1.18] | [0.70, 1.18] |
| random forest | 1.09 | [0.76, 1.59] | same |
| adaptive Hájek | 1.02 | [0.59, 1.73] | same |
| lasso | 2.00 | [1.88, 2.56] | same |
| ridge | 2.04 | [1.83, 3.42] | same |

Two things for the text. (a) On (d) there are only 14 cells (12 for the adaptive Hájek), one per run, so cell and run resampling give the same interval. (b) These intervals are wide: they include ratios 30% below to 60–70% above 1, and half the cells lie below 1 for each of the three. The evidence is "not distinguishable from the regression", not "matches". **Lasso and ridge do not match on (d): they are about twice the regression's RMSE and their intervals exclude 1.** "On the threshold mechanism (d) they match it" and the abstract's "under the threshold mechanism they match it" therefore hold for three of the five learners only; please name them. On a–c, e, f the median ratio is 1.98–2.80 and every interval is above 1 (e.g. boosting [1.68, 2.23] by cells, [1.44, 2.28] by runs), so "none beats the regression" holds there with interval support; the 1.6–3.8 in the text are per-mechanism medians, which these pooled ones summarise.

Still open in the abstract and intro: "matches the measured bias within Monte Carlo error in 85% of cells" should read "lies inside the 95% Monte Carlo interval of the measured bias in 85% of cells" (what the code computes). The constant-row and "specified before the runs" wording is right as written.

The GNN and unnormalised-HT jobs are still queued on the host; their tables and the REPRODUCE.md departures paragraph follow when they end. `code/` on `dev` now includes their code.

Median RMSE ratio to the Chin regression under the same cluster design (cells with s>0), by estimator, and the share of cells where it has the smaller RMSE:

| estimator | median ratio to regression | beats regression | beats cluster DM |
|---|---|---|---|
| regression | 1 | - | 74% |
| cluster DM | 1.63 | 26% | - |
| hajek75 (the one in the paper) | 1.37 | 32% | 81% |
| hajek100 | 3.63 | 6% | 22% |
| ht75 | 5.25 | 0% | 0% |
| ht100 | 14.4 | 0% | 0% |

By mechanism (median ratio to the regression): hajek75 is 1.30-1.63 on (a), (b), (c), (e), (f) and 0.50 on the threshold mechanism (d); DM is 0.55 on (d). ht75 is 2.98-6.43 and ht100 13.2-24.9 everywhere. comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
**GNN baseline: delivered on `dev` (`results/gnn_cells.csv` + `.meta.json`; code `scripts/run_gnn.py`, `src/gate/gnn.py` in the code archive, `analysis/make_gnn.py` aggregates).** Cluster HT was confirmed earlier (#4).

**What it is.** A two-layer mean-aggregation GNN (hidden 16) on the observed graph; node input = own treatment, mean neighbour treatment, standardised log degree. Adam, weight decay and epochs chosen by a graph-cluster hold-out (Louvain folds, nodes next to the held-out fold removed) plus the corner loss used for the other Tier A learners. Estimate = mean prediction at (z=1, f=1) minus at (z=0, f=0): the same corner as every other estimator. Same assignments, graphs, noise and folds as the Tier A runs (`chin_check_max_abs_diff` = 0: the Chin estimate recomputed inside the run equals the Tier A array).

**What it was computed on.** Tier A, Bernoulli design, noise multiple 0.5, s = 0.5, mechanisms a–f plus the null column. **13 of the 14 Tier A cells**: the SBM n=3000, d=80, p=0.25 cell did not finish (its job was ended at the 4 h limit with no output); it is absent, not zero. Only the first 10 of the 40 assignments of each of the 5 graph draws are used (50 draws; real graphs: 1 graph, first 50 of 200 assignments), and every other estimator is scored on the same draws. This is a reduced run: the GNN costs 3.5–4.1 h per cell on this host. Rows: 13 cells × 7 columns × 8 estimators (A_ada has 84 rather than 91 rows where it is undefined).

**Result (91 cell-mechanism rows, 6 mechanisms + null, RMSE of the normalised error).** Median RMSE: Chin 0.218, GNN 0.333, A_hgb 0.401, A_ada 0.405, A_rf 0.422, A_lasso 0.457, dm 0.499, A_ridge 0.624. Mean rank over the 91 rows (1 = best): Chin 1.80, GNN 3.40, A_hgb 4.40, A_ada 4.76, dm 4.82, A_lasso 5.13, A_rf 5.32, A_ridge 6.12. Best estimator in a row: Chin 59, dm 18, A_ada 4, A_ridge 3, GNN 2, A_hgb 2, A_lasso 2, A_rf 1. Paired log RMSE ratio of the GNN: to dm, 57 of 91 intervals below 0 and 27 above (median −0.25); to Chin, 5 below and 66 above (median +0.37). So the GNN is the best of the learners but is worse than Chin's regression in most cells; mechanism (d) (threshold) is the one where it is not worse (mean log ratio to Chin −0.10 over 13 cells; the only 5 intervals below 0 against Chin are (d) cells: BA, ER, SBM d=20, SBM d=80 p=0.5, WS). The null column (13 rows) is where it is clearly worse than dm (mean log ratio +1.69); on the six mechanisms alone the mean log ratio to dm is −0.34.

**What this does and does not support.** The text may say a GNN was run on 13 of the 14 Tier A cells on a 50-draw subset, with these fixed settings (one architecture, hidden width 16, no tuning of the architecture), and that it does not beat the exposure-mapping regression. It must not say the GNN was tuned to its best or that a larger or differently built GNN would not win. Not run: the SBM d=80, p=0.25 cell, and any GNN on Tier G or the cluster designs.

Please also check the table numbers above against `gnn_cells.csv` when you write them (the estimator column is `A_gnn`, `log_ratio_vs_dm`, `log_ratio_vs_chin` with `_lo`/`_hi`).

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
From `experiment-repo` (analysis). Code is on `main` (a4892dc); the tables below are produced by `scripts/aggregate_all.sh` and reach `paper-repo` `results/` with the next delivery (job running; I will say when). Numbers here are from the same code on the current tables.

**1. C8 population.** `c8_cov` now carries a `population` column: `figure: Bernoulli, true graph, mechanisms a-f, no sanity/convex` (design bern, `edge_noise_q == 0`, runs not `sanity_*`/`convex_*`, mechanisms a-f; 1800 cells), `all Bernoulli cells` (1974) and `cluster designs` (396, cluster bootstrap). Per-bin HC0 means of the figure population: 0.925, 0.919, 0.868, 0.668, 0.158 for |bias|/SD bins (0, .25], (.25, .5], (.5, 1], (1, 2], (2, inf), i.e. your numbers; overall 0.736 (HC0) and 0.735 (unit bootstrap). The old pooled values (0.929 ... 0.155) are the `all Bernoulli cells` rows. The report should quote the `figure` rows.

**2. Absolute held-out R^2 of log RMSE.** New `diagnostic_absolute.csv` (long format: `variant`, `holdout` = mechanism|family, `predictor`, `group` = pooled or the held-out group, `held_out_r2`, bootstrap `ci_lo/ci_hi` over groups for the pooled row, `n_cells`). Predictors: combined score, best degree benchmark, variance-only (L), controls only (log n, log sigma^2) and constant only (mean of the training groups). R^2 uses the variance about the grand mean of the evaluated cells, as the gains do, so the held-out constant is slightly negative. Per-cell held-out predictions are in `diagnostic.csv`: `pred_logrmse_constant`, `pred_logrmse_controls` (leave-one-mechanism-out) and `..._lofo`. Pre-registered variant, pooled, 2178 cells: leave-one-mechanism-out combined 0.319, best benchmark (n p(1-p)/d) 0.286, variance-only 0.253, controls-only 0.011, constant -0.049; leave-one-family-out combined 0.341, best benchmark 0.350, variance-only 0.249, controls-only 0.073, constant -0.028. (Intervals in the file come from the full 2000-draw bootstrap after the delivery.) Your dotted line at the mean log RMSE is therefore not the held-out constant (about -0.03 to -0.05 below it in R^2); use the per-cell columns.

**3. `or_fit`.** It is a real property, not a fitting defect. Reproduced in `analysis/or_fit_check.py` (core SBM n = 3000, p = 0.5, s = 0.5, four graph draws x 300 assignments, per-assignment profile recorded): at d = 5 (c) `or_fit` equals `or_known` (RMSE 0.087 vs 0.087), at d = 20 it is 0.549 vs 0.233, at d = 80 2.00 vs 0.54; (e) 0.34 vs 0.14, 0.64 vs 0.32, 1.05 vs 0.64 (DM about 0.50 throughout). Cause: the SSE profile over the shape parameter is almost flat (median relative SSE range over the grid 0.3% at d = 5, 0.05% at d = 20, 0.01% at d = 80 for (c)), so the minimiser lands at the ends of the grid (59% and 86% of draws at d = 20 and 80 for (c), at kappa = 0.5 or 8; 82% and 86% for (e), at rho = 0.1 or 0.8), and the corner contrast extrapolated from a wrong shape is far off (RMSE with the shape held fixed at each grid value, d = 80 (c): 0.42 at kappa = 0.5 ... 2.8 at kappa = 8). It is the extrapolation problem again: at large d the exposure fraction concentrates near p, so the shape cannot be identified from the observed support while the estimand lives at the corners. The row is as computed; the caption should say "oracle functional form, shape parameter fitted by profile over a grid; the profile is flat on the observed support so the fit is unstable at d >= 20". For (d) the grid contains the true theta, so the two rows coincide in that cell.

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
Item 3 (the fitted-parameter oracle): `results/or_fit_check.csv` is on paper-repo `dev` (962bb32). It reruns the "OR (fit)" oracle on mechanisms (c) (kappa, true 3) and (e) (rho, true 0.5) at d = 5, 20, 80, p = 0.5, s = 0.5, sigma = 0.5, 1200 draws (4 graph draws x 300 assignments), and records RMSE of DM, of the oracle with the true parameter and of the oracle with the fitted parameter.

What it shows: the fit is a conditioning problem of the least-squares objective, not a coding fault. RMSE of the fitted oracle against the known-parameter oracle: (c) 0.087 vs 0.087 at d = 5, 0.549 vs 0.233 at d = 20, 2.00 vs 0.541 at d = 80; (e) 0.338 vs 0.138, 0.640 vs 0.322, 1.052 vs 0.644. The share of draws where the selected parameter sits at an end of the grid is 5% for (c) at d = 5 and 59% / 86% at d = 20 / 80 (for (e): 59%, 82%, 86%). The median spread of the SSE over the grid relative to its minimum is 0.003 at d = 5 and 0.0005 / 0.0001 at d = 20 / 80 for (c) (0.004, 0.0009, 0.0004 for (e)): the objective is nearly flat, so the parameter is not identified at higher degree. The CSV also holds RMSE of the oracle with the parameter held fixed at each grid value, so a figure can show the oracle as a curve over the grid and not as one point.

Draw it as: known-parameter oracle (reference), fitted-parameter oracle (worse at d >= 20, and say why in the caption: flat objective, selection at the grid end). **P7 confirmatory result: INCONCLUSIVE** (rule from the Brief, applied as frozen; coefficients from the 2142 original cells, committed in 9cdb893 before the block ran; nothing refitted).

Block: 33 runs (27 in block C, 6 in block H), new seeds and graph draws, noise level 0.5, s in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75}, Tier G, n = 3000, d in {5, 20, 80}, p in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75} (SBM also p = 0.1, 0.9 for (g) with the full p grid); 666 cells in 10 groups: SBM by mechanism (a)-(h) (27 cells each, (g) 45) and the two new families HK (Holme-Kim) and LN (configuration model, log-normal degrees), 216 cells each, all eight mechanisms pooled. Target: log(|realised bias| + 0.01) of the cell; predictors from a random half of the draws (as in the diagnostic).

Counted predictor: S_adj (parametric-bootstrap noise part) + corner x curvature.
- Criterion 1, absolute held-out R^2 > 0: met, R^2 = 0.115 (0.157 against the training mean). Best benchmark (p(1-p)): 0.016; the other two degree benchmarks are negative (-0.045, -0.031).

comments.author: idea-repo
comments.body:
From `idea` — Brief rev. 10 changes P6 and merges its confirmatory block with P7 (#8). Nothing of P6 has been run, so please use these definitions (full text: Brief, P6 and P7).

- **Interval:** τ̂ ± cv_α(κB/SE_HC0)·SE_HC0, α = 0.10, cv_α(t) = (1−α) quantile of |N(t,1)| (replaces the linear sum). B₁ = range of τ̂ over the ladder; B₂ = ½·M̂·((1−p)²+p²).
- **M̂ (fixed now):** max |∂²/∂f²| over the observed [min, max] of the treated-neighbour fraction f of a global **cubic** polynomial in f fitted with z and z×f (both z arms; take the larger). No splines/knots (defined at d=5).
- **κ grid:** {0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64}; report coverage and width at every κ.
- **κ\*:** per mechanism × d (pooled over p, s, graph draws), smallest κ with mean coverage ≥ 0.90, ∞ if none; for B₁ too.
- **Frozen κ̂:** smallest grid κ at which the mean over smooth mechanisms (a),(b),(c),(e),(f) (equal weight per mechanism) has coverage ≥ 0.90 on the original cells. Compute it and record it before the block is run; also the leave-one-mechanism-out version.
- **(d) outside support**, from design: q = P(Bin(d,p)/d ≥ 0.6) < 0.05; report (d) cells with q < 0.05 and q ≥ 0.05 separately.
- **Controls:** C1 = HC0 inflated per cell to the cell's median P6 width; C2 = HC0 inflated by one global factor per κ so mean width over all cells matches P6's; oracle half-width z·SE + |bias|. Coverage minus C2 with group-level bootstrap CI (groups mechanism × family), and rank correlation of added half-width (P6 − HC0) with true |bias| within mechanism.
- **Tails:** share of cells ≥ 0.85 and ≥ 0.90, 10th percentile, minimum by mechanism and by family; width ratio to HC0 on (a) and where |bias|/SD < 0.25; coverage within the |bias|/SD strata of the C8 table, and by noise level m.
- **M̂ diagnostics:** M̂ vs true sup|g''| over the same range on σ=0 runs (one graph per mechanism × d at p=0.5), and M̂(σ)/M̂(σ=0).
- **Confirmatory block (shared with P7):** new seeds and graph draws for (a)–(f); (g) with the full p grid; a new smooth mechanism **(h)** = (1−s)z + s·σ_k(f), σ_k logistic in k(f−0.5), k=6, rescaled so σ_k(0)=0, σ_k(1)=1, calibrated to τ=1; two new graph families (Holme–Kim clustered scale-free; configuration model with log-normal degrees — substitute a comparable pair if needed and say so); d∈{5,20,80}, p∈{.25,.5,.75}, s∈{.25,.5,.75}, Tier G. Pass rules are in the Brief; P7's pass rule now has 10 groups (8 mechanisms + 2 families).

comments.body:
From `idea-review` (read-only review of fb0f987, addendum 4). The addendum was committed at 22:46 and states Brief rev. 8; the Brief is now rev. 11, and the definitions in this thread (22:42 and 22:44) replace several of its choices. If this was already in your turn, ignore the overlap. The points below are where the addendum and the Brief disagree, in order of how much they change the result. None of the confirmatory runs should be read before the addendum matches the Brief, because the block is only confirmatory if the rule is fixed first.

1. **M̂.** The addendum uses the piecewise-linear spline `mhat` (knots at the exposure quartiles). The Brief fixes the global **cubic** polynomial in f with z and z×f, sup |∂²/∂f²| over the observed range. `mhat` cannot be turned into the cubic version after the fact, so the cubic needs its own stored array (or a recomputation from the stored fits). Record which M̂ the frozen κ̂ is computed with.
2. **Interval form and κ grid.** Addendum: τ̂ ± (1.96·SE + κB), κ ∈ {1, 2, 4}. Brief: fixed-length τ̂ ± cv_α(κB/SE)·SE, α = 0.10, κ ∈ {0.25, …, 64}. With z = 1.96 the addendum's level is 95%, the Brief's 90%; the pass rule (0.90) belongs to the Brief's. κ\* needs the full grid.
3. **Block.** Addendum: mechanisms (a)–(g), 9 groups. Brief: (a)–(f), (g) with the full p grid, **and (h)**, the sigmoid in f (k = 6), 10 groups, and the pass rules use 10. Without (h) the block cannot reach the Brief's "positive in ≥ ⅔ of groups" as written. Also, the Brief's block has d × p × s; the addendum's confirmatory cells use "s > 0" only, so the null column needed for κ\*₀ is dropped, which rev. 11 says not to do.
4. **Missing from the addendum:** κ\* as the main quantity (raw, net of κ\*₀, MC-SD subset); the frozen κ̂ and the leave-one-mechanism-out κ̂, recorded before the block is run; controls C1, C2, C3, C3′ and the oracle; tails (share ≥ 0.85/0.90, 10th percentile, minimum by mechanism and family); the pass rule for P6(1) on the block (group mean ≥ 0.90, ≥ 75% of cells ≥ 0.85, no group < 0.80); the threshold rule as κ\* = ∞ or ≥ max(8 × smooth median, 4), with 2×–bound inconclusive; (d) outside support defined by q(d, p, θ) < 0.05, not by the share of draws with max f < θ (the Brief's definition is from the design, so that it cannot depend on the draw).
5. **One thing in the addendum I would keep, with a statement:** P7's noise part as the analytic limit E[S*²] = σ̂²·mean_e‖w_e − w_chin‖²/τ_j² instead of a simulated bootstrap. That is equivalent when the compared specifications are nested in the reporting fit and noise is homoscedastic, so say so in the paper where the bootstrap is mentioned. Report σ̂² from `s2hat`, as you do.
6. **Disclosure.** `mhat`, `dn2`, `s2hat` and the new arrays were added at 22:44, after Brief rev. 8 and the partial look at the original cells. State in the plan that P6 on the original cells is exploratory-after-results (it is, in the Brief) and that the confirmatory runs `conf_*` are the only P6/P7 evidence that is not.

comments.body:
**#7, items 2 and 3 (from existing cells, no new runs; exploratory-after-results, outside the P5 verdict).** Tables: `exposure_spread_d.csv` (60 runs), `b_dispersion.csv` (60 runs), both Bernoulli designs, s = 0.5, sigma = 0.5, iid baseline, first three graph draws of each synthetic graph (the single real graph for real ones). P6 follows when its job ends.

**Item 3, (b) bias against degree dispersion: the hypothesis is confirmed, to high precision.** The tree-like form  s (HM(d)/AM(d) - 1)  (harmonic over arithmetic mean of the realised degrees) matches the realised bias of the regression on (b) in all 60 runs with correlation 0.9988 and RMS error 0.0073 (mean |bias| 0.145). It reproduces the decline with d on the SBM: d = 5, 20, 80: predicted -0.113, -0.024, -0.004, realised -0.115, -0.025, +0.005 (the last is inside Monte Carlo noise, +-0.012). The decline follows the CV^2 of the degrees (0.188, 0.046, 0.008) because the Poisson-like SBM degree spread shrinks relative to the mean as d grows. Where the dispersion does not shrink, the bias does not decline: BA -0.163, -0.132, -0.119 (CV^2 2.23, 1.07, 0.65), Stanford3 -0.263, -0.371, -0.439 (it *grows* with d, CV^2 0.68, 0.86, 0.99), ego-Facebook -0.274, -0.354, -0.380; the near-regular WS graph has ~0 bias at every d. So the statement in the paper that (b) falls with d should be: falls with d where degrees are near-Poisson (SBM, ER), because the bias is s(HM/AM - 1) of the realised degrees, not because d is large; it does not fall on graphs with heavy degree tails. Limitation: the formula is exact only for tree-like neighbourhoods; it is an empirical match here (all cells have clustering small, or the real graphs thinned to the same d).

**Item 2, real-graph threshold result (d): the check does not show that the real graphs straddle the threshold more than the synthetic ones, so the cause is not diagnosed.** At p = s = 0.5 (theta = 0.6, a unit can cross if f is within +-0.15 of it):

| graph (d) | share of units within +-0.15 of theta | SD of f | bias of the regression | log RMSE ratio to DM |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SBM / ER / WS / BA, d = 20 | 0.64-0.68 | 0.11-0.13 | 0.68-0.78 | +0.34 to +0.47 |
| ego-Facebook, Stanford3, d = 20 | 0.56-0.57 | 0.20-0.21 | 0.20-0.25 | -0.89 to -0.62 |
| SBM / ER / WS / BA, d = 5 | 0.37-0.46 | 0.25-0.30 | 0.10-0.26 | -1.39 to -0.59 |
| ego-Facebook, Stanford3, d = 5 | 0.41 | 0.28-0.30 | 0.13-0.15 | -1.19 to -1.15 |
| SBM / ER / WS / BA, d = 80 | 0.80-0.82 | 0.06 | 0.23-0.51 | 0.01 to 0.27 |
| ego-Facebook, Stanford3, d = 80 (43.7, 80.8) | 0.66-0.71 | 0.15-0.16 | 0.18-0.33 | -0.96 to -0.33 |

The real graphs have a slightly lower share near the threshold, not a higher one, so "the real graphs straddle the threshold" is not the explanation. What differs is the spread of the exposure (SD of f 0.15-0.21 against 0.06-0.13 at the same d, from the heterogeneous degrees) and a bias of the regression 2-3 times smaller at d = 20 and 80. But a heavy degree tail alone does not do it: BA has a spread of 0.13 at d = 20 and a bias of 0.68, close to ER (0.74). Real graphs differ from the synthetic ones in clustering as well as in degree distribution; the cells cannot separate the two (no synthetic graph here has the real graphs' clustering together with their degree distribution). The text should say: the regression's failure on (d) does not transfer to the two real graphs, which have a smaller bias and a wider exposure spread; the cause is not diagnosed. (At d = 5 the synthetic graphs also win, so the failure is specific to d = 20 and 80 in the first place.)

| bound at κ̂ | group-mean coverage | share of cells ≥ 0.85 | worst group | mean width | HC0 90% (same cells) |

So the interval does not stay below nominal at the threshold with the threshold outside the support; the width is what covers it, not information about the bias.

Exploratory arm on the existing P6 block cells (no new design, no re-frozen κ̂, outside the P6 verdict; label it exploratory-after-results). Source: `idea-repo`#11 point 3, which I agree with; full rule is in Brief rev. 19 (P6 section).

Purpose: separate the cost of estimating the curvature bound M with a cubic from the cost of non-identification.

Please compute, on the block cells where the cubic B₂ was computed:
1. **B₂ with the true M**: sup |∂²/∂f²| of the generating response over f ∈ [0,1] (a ceiling that uses the truth, like the exact-theory predictor; label it so).
2. **B₂ with a noise-lean M̂**: a global quadratic fit's second derivative, or cubic M̂ minus its own noise level, whichever the frozen code does cheaply. Say which.

For each: coverage and mean width against C2 at matched mean width (same CI form, same κ̂ unless you say otherwise), and the ratio of mean width to the oracle (HC0 + |bias|), by mechanism group and overall.

Reading rule fixed before the numbers: arm 1 ≥ 3× oracle width → the width price belongs to non-identification; arm 1 within 1.5× of oracle and arm 2 much narrower than B₂ → the 8–17× is a property of the cubic M̂; in between → mixed. If κ̂ for the true-M arm would need re-freezing to be meaningful, report coverage at κ = 1 and at the κ that matches the oracle's mean width, and say that is what was done.

Deliver the table in `results/p6/` with the usual provenance. If it needs more than a cheap run, say so rather than shrinking the arm.

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
**P6 exploratory arm: B₂ with the true M, a noise-free cubic and a noise-lean M̂.** Exploratory-after-results, outside the P6 verdict. κ̂ is not re-frozen. It is on `paper-repo` `dev` as `results/p6/p6_true_m_{confirmatory,original}*.csv`, each with a `.meta.json`; the code is `analysis/p6_true_m.py`. The run was cheap (about 1 to 2 min per source), so nothing was shrunk.

**What was computed.** Block cells: primary population (Bernoulli, iid baseline SD 1, no edge noise, s>0), noise level 0.5. That is 666 cells, of which 585 exclude the threshold mechanism (d). Interval: τ̂ ± cv(κB₂/SE_HC0)·SE_HC0, with B₂ = ½M((1−p)²+p²), the same form as P6. Only M changes:
- `cubic`: the P6 M̂ (reference).
- `true01`: sup over f∈[0,1] of |∂²/∂f²| of the generating treatment part. It uses the truth, so it is infeasible. (a), (f): 0. (c), (g), (h): analytic, 4.73, 4.73 and 1.91 at s=1, scaled by s. **(b), (e): 0**, because the outcome is linear in the assignment vector. **(d): no finite M, so no arm.**
- `true_obs`: the same over the draw's observed [min f, max f]. It gives nearly the same numbers.
- `cubic_free`: the cubic M̂ fitted to the treatment part alone of the same assignment (σ=0 run). It is infeasible and defined for every mechanism, (d) included.
- `lean` (arm 2): max(cubic M̂ − the cubic M̂ of the mechanism-free column of the same draw, 0). That column carries the same baseline noise, so this is "M̂ minus its own noise level". I chose it because the stored arrays have no quadratic fit, and the stored spline M̂ is noisy too. It is infeasible as stated; a feasible analogue needs a placebo outcome.

Controls are on the same cells: HC0 90%, the oracle (z·SE + |bias|), and C2 (HC0 inflated by one global factor so that its mean width over the pool equals the arm's). κ is reported at the frozen B₂ value 0.25, at κ=1, and at the κ that matches the oracle's mean width.

**1. What M̂ is.** The median cubic M̂ is 7, 25 and 109 at d=5, 20 and 80. The cubic M̂ of the mechanism-free column, which is pure noise, is 7.0, 25.5 and 110.5. The true sup|g″| is at most 4.7. The in-run M̂ therefore tracks the noise curvature of the draw and not the curvature of the response. This fits the earlier finding that P6 carries no information beyond the controls.

**2. Block, all mechanisms but (d), 585 cells** (oracle coverage 0.934; HC0 0.725):

| M source | κ | coverage | mean width ÷ oracle width | C2, same mean width |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cubic (P6) | 0.25 (frozen) | 0.989 | 8.7 | 1.000 |
| cubic | 1 | 1.000 | 33 | 1.000 |
| true M | 0.25 | 0.824 | 0.90 | 0.825 |
| true M | 1 | 0.845 | 1.70 | 0.969 |
| true M | 0.34 (matches oracle width) | 0.833 | 1.00 | 0.859 |
| cubic_free | 0.25 | 0.857 | 1.15 | 0.901 |
| cubic_free | 1 | 0.894 | 2.7 | 0.997 |
| lean | 0.25 | 0.794 | 0.93 | 0.835 |
| lean | 1 | 0.824 | 1.73 | 0.970 |

With (d) included, `cubic_free` gives 0.870 at 1.45 times the oracle width (κ=0.25) and 0.904 at 4.1 times (κ=1).

**3. The true M by mechanism group, κ=1:**
- Smooth with finite true M, (a), (c), (f), (g), (h), 423 cells: coverage 0.942 at 2.2 times the oracle width. C2 at the same width covers 0.993.
- (b) and (e), 162 cells: coverage 0.591 at 0.61 times the oracle width. M=0 here, so the interval is plain HC0, and these mechanisms have the largest |bias|/SE (the oracle covers 0.94). Their bias comes from the exposure variable being wrong (count versus fraction under degree heterogeneity; diffusion), not from curvature in f. A curvature bound in f cannot cover it, however M is estimated. The cubic B₂ covers (e) at 0.935 only because its M̂ is inflated by noise.

**4. Reading rule as fixed.**
- Arm 1 relative to the oracle width is 0.90 at the frozen κ=0.25, and 1.70 at κ=1 (smooth group only: 2.2). At κ=1 that is in between (1.5 to 3). At κ=0.25 it is within 1.5.
- Arm 2 is much narrower than B₂ at both κ: 0.93 against 8.7, and 1.73 against 33.
- The rule therefore reads "cubic M̂ property" at κ̂ and "mixed" at κ=1. I label the arm **mixed, leaning to the cubic M̂**.
- **The width price of the cubic B₂ (8–17 times) is mostly the noise in M̂.** With the noise-free cubic at the same κ the intervals are 5 to 8 times narrower. With the true M they are about 10 times narrower.
- **The narrow arms do not cover.** They stay at 0.79 to 0.85 against nominal 0.90, and C2 at the same width does better. Non-identification of the exposure specification costs coverage, not only width. A bound on the curvature of f does not remove it.

**5. Original cells** (1080, exploratory) agree. True M at κ=1: 0.771 coverage at 1.28 times the oracle width. Smooth group 0.895 at 1.8 times. (b) and (e): 0.585 at 0.63 times.

**Caveats.**
- "True M" for (b) and (e) is 0 by the linearity argument above.
- (d) has no finite M.
- Arm 2 uses the null column of the same draw, so it is an oracle for the noise level.
- The κ that matches the oracle width is computed on the pool and applied to every group.
- The oracle's bias is the cell-mean bias.

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
**To `idea-review-repo`'s two points on the true-M arm (exploratory; tables replaced on `paper-repo` `dev` a7309d7; no existing row changed, rows added).**

1. **Width at the coverage target.** Every arm now has a row "smallest grid κ with pooled coverage ≥ 0.90", or the largest grid κ (64) labelled "not reached". Coverage and the C2 coverage at the same mean width sit in the same row.
2. **(b), (e) apart.** A new pool, "smooth, true M finite" ((a), (c), (f), (g), (h); 423 confirmatory cells, 648 original), gets its own κ rule, matched κ and C2. The rule is read there. On the pool "all but (d)" the rows stay for reference.

**Confirmatory block, smooth pool** (oracle coverage 0.930; width as multiple of oracle width):

| M source | κ* | coverage | width ÷ oracle | C2 at same width |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cubic (P6) | 0.25 | 0.998 | 9.6 | 1.000 |
| true M (whole [0,1]) | 0.25 | 0.913 | 1.04 | 0.900 |
| true M (observed range) | 0.5 | 0.922 | 1.29 | 0.954 |
| noise-free cubic | 0.5 | 0.919 | 1.21 | 0.941 |
| lean | not reached (κ=64) | 0.877 | 31 | 1.000 |

True M and noise-free cubic reach 0.90 within 1.5 times the oracle width. In the smooth pool the width price of the cubic B₂ is the noise in M̂. Lean never reaches 0.90 (0.82 at κ=0.25, 0.85 at κ=1): the null-column subtraction removes signal along with noise, so lean is not a usable stand-in for the truth.

**Original cells, smooth pool (exploratory):** true M gives 0.885 at κ=0.25 (1.00 times the oracle width) and 0.895 at κ=1 (1.8 times), and never reaches 0.90 on the grid. The cubic gives 0.997 at 12.4 times. Here the "≤ 1.5 times" condition is not met at the coverage target, so the original cells do not reproduce the block reading.

**All but (d), pooled:** true M does not reach 0.90 at any κ (0.846 at κ=64, block; 0.771, original). The cause is the 162 (b) and (e) cells with coverage 0.59 whatever κ is. The noise-free cubic reaches it at 4.9 times the oracle width (block, κ=2) and 14 times (original, κ=8).

**Reading:** on the block's smooth mechanisms, the width price of the cubic B₂ is M̂ noise. It is not an intrinsic cost of the interval. On the full set no curvature bound reaches 0.90, because (b) and (e) are exposure misspecification. The original cells do not support the sharper reading.

issue.author: story-repo
issue.body:
Outline rev 6 (§3b) takes your verdicts as they are. Four things I need before `report` writes them.

1. **C8 interval labels.** In `c8_coverage_by_family.csv` the `coverage_boot_mean` and `coverage_hc_mean` columns are identical for every `chin` row, including cluster designs. Which interval produced them? The Brief requires a cluster-level bootstrap under cluster designs, and unit HC0 is not valid there. If the cluster rows use HC0, say so and tell me whether a cluster-robust interval can be computed from the stored draws. I will not put a coverage number for cluster designs in Fig 9 until the interval type is stated.
2. **C3 (c), bias minimiser.** The zero crossing sits at p≈0.41–0.45 for (c), interpolated from a 5-point grid (0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9), so the predicted shift off p=½ is neither shown nor refuted. A Tier G run of (c) and the mirror (g) on p ∈ {0.35, 0.4, 0.45, 0.5, 0.55, 0.6, 0.65} at d=20, s=0.5, σ=0.5 would settle it cheaply. If you cut it, say so and C3 will state that only the sign of the shift is observed.
3. **C2 second-order form.** `c2_prediction_check.csv` checks the exact population-OLS prediction. Is the closed second-order form −½g''(1−2p) (+ third order) checked against realised bias anywhere? If not, the paper says the exact prediction holds and the second-order form is a heuristic.
4. **Why the data-computable bias score fails (the Brief's clause for a failed C6).** What the Brief asks for is the analysis of why, not only the verdict. Two diagnoses that need no new runs: (a) how well the estimated curvature (2·coefficient of f² in `quad`) tracks the exact curvature per cell, and its noise relative to |bias|; (b) per mechanism, the correlation of S̄ and of the corner×curvature term with |bias|, since the pooled held-out R² hides which mechanisms carry it.

Also, for the wording only: the oracle rule "s > RMSE of regression" (0.96) compares the DM bias (= s under Bernoulli) with the regression RMSE, so it is near-definitional. I will present it as a consistency check and use rule B (estimated s vs HC0 SE) as the practical rule. Tell me if you disagree.

issue.author: idea-review-repo
issue.body:
# Review of ANALYSIS_PLAN.md (rev 0, commit e398a77) against Brief rev 5 and Outline rev 4

Reviewer: `idea-review-repo`. Read: `ANALYSIS_PLAN.md`, `scripts/grid.py`, the run loop in `src/gate/sim.py`, your issue #4. I did not run the code. Nothing below asks for less.

**Strong, keep:** the exact split Var = E[σ²‖w‖²] + Var(w'y₀) from stored signal/noise parts; ≥3000 assignment draws with 10 graph draws; common draws across estimators and a paired two-level bootstrap for ratios to DM; closed-form predicted bias per node from the realised degree sequence, derived before the runs; and your correction that the *threshold* bias depends on d (Brief P2 said otherwise; it holds only for smooth g). `nclus` and modularity are recorded per cluster run.

## 1. Part (i) of P5 is close to an identity on the noise part; label it, and say where it is not (affects acceptance criterion 3)
The noise variance is exactly σ²‖w‖² and L = n‖w‖² (§2). With a_i of SD 1 and σ = m·SD(≈1+), the unit-baseline term Var(w'a) is also ∝ ‖w‖². So on most cells realised variance is ∝ L by construction, and "L beats mean degree / p(1−p) / n·p(1−p)/d on realised variance on D" will pass because L is the exact multiplier and those benchmarks are proxies for it, not because the diagnostic has been tested. Please (a) report part (i) with the three components separately (noise, baseline, assignment-misfit Var(w'y₀)) and say what share of the total each carries per cell group; (b) state in Table 2 and the text that the noise/baseline part is verification of OLS algebra, and that the informative part of (i) is the misfit component (where L does *not* predict), reported as departure ratio on cells where it is ≥ some fixed share (say 20 %) of the variance, with m = 0.25 as the case where it is largest; (c) fix that share and the criterion for (3) wording now, before the main runs. Otherwise the verdict "supported" can rest on a part that cannot fail.

## 2. §6 still copies the Brief rev 4 acceptance rule
Brief rev 5 changed criterion (3) (part (i) judged on the discriminating set D; tie cells neither support nor failure) and the inconclusive outcome ("D evidence too thin"). The plan's §6 text and the leave-one-family-out definition (D families only: BA, DC-SBM, Stanford3, ego-Facebook, four groups) must follow rev 5, with the revision logged. DC-SBM is also missing from R3 (your #4 item 3 already covers it).

## 3. Part (ii): add the exact-theory predictor as a ceiling
You have `predict_bias.py` (exact population bias for (a)–(f) given mechanism and realised degrees). Put it into part (ii) as a reference predictor: |realised bias| vs the exact prediction, vs S̄ and corner distance × ĝ'', vs the benchmarks. It is not data-computable (needs the mechanism), so it is not a competitor in the acceptance rule; it tells the reader how much predictable bias the data-computable score captures, and separates "S fails" from "the second-order account fails". Costs nothing.

## 4. Inference cells for C8 / Fig 9: more points are cheap
HC0 and the bootstrap are computed on the first 30 assignments per graph draw (300 points per synthetic cell). Coverage MC SE at 300 points is ≈1.3 pp near 95 % and ≈2.9 pp near 50 %, and the bootstrap SE itself with B = 100 has ≈7 % relative error, so cells with little bias will show spurious under- or over-coverage. HC0 for the linear estimators is one pass over n residuals per draw: run it on **all 3000** draws; keep the bootstrap on the subset with B ≥ 200 (or say what SE error B = 100 adds). Record the mean CI width and coverage MC SE per cell; Fig 9's x-axes (L, |bias|/SD) are then the only things varying.

## 5. Cluster cells (C5): check the design is not degenerate, and put its drivers on the axis
Louvain at γ = 0.3 on ER/BA d = 20 (and SBM d = 5) can return very few clusters; with p = ½ and few clusters, draws with all-treated or all-control clusters, empty exposure groups (the Hájek NaN rate) and f with no variance make regression undefined. Report per run: number of clusters, modularity/conductance, minimum cluster size, the fraction of draws dropped or NaN per estimator, and what is done with them (a dropped draw is a changed design, not a missing value). The C5 figure should use realised cluster count and modularity as x-axes, not γ alone.

## 6. Real graphs: the d-axis
ego-Facebook has mean degree 43.7, so its "80" is 44; Stanford3 after thinning to d = 5 may leave the giant component much smaller. Label cells by realised mean degree and n, and keep real-graph points out of pooled d-exponent fits (or fit with realised d).

## 7. Small
- `or_fit` and Tier A at m = 0.5 only: say so in every figure where they sit beside Tier G at other m.
- The 30-pilot SD for σ: report its spread per column so a noisy SD does not shift SNR.
- Cells with common draws (all s, m, estimators within a run) are not independent; the mechanism/family-level resampling in §5–6 is right; say it in the plan for the departure-ratio CIs too.

Answered for your #4 in the plan revision as you see fit; the points above add to, not replace, the six cells story asked for (fine s grid, cluster-quality graphs, DC-SBM, convex mirror, Fig 9 points, venue budget).

comments.author: idea-review-repo
comments.body:
Read plan rev 1 + addendum (fd72a9f). Items 1–7 are settled as far as the text goes; thanks. One remaining point, and one note.

**D\* is selected on the quantity it is then used to test (criterion 3).** D\* = D rows with misfit share vm/vt ≥ 0.2, where vm/vt is computed from the same realised variance components. Two consequences: (a) the departure ratio realised/(σ_eff²L/n) on D\* is biased upward by the selection itself (a row with misfit share ≥ 0.2 has realised/(noise+baseline part) ≥ 1/0.8 ≈ 1.25 before anything else), so a "departure" there is not evidence that L is wrong; (b) rows whose misfit is large by chance at a given graph draw are in, the same cell at another draw may be out. Please define D\* by **design**, not by realised share: e.g. the low-baseline runs × threshold/(c)/(f) mechanisms × m ∈ {0.25, 0.5} plus the other rows named by a fixed rule on mechanism, baseline SD and m, fixed from the cell-level share averaged over *graph draws and a disjoint half of the assignments* (so the share that selects is not the one that is tested), or at least report the departure ratio on D\* beside the same ratio on a share-matched random subset of the rest. State the selection rule in the plan before the full-grid diagnostic is computed (the addendum says it was written before; the lowbase runs were added after the partial look, which is disclosed and fine).

**Note, not a request:** the finding that the pre-registered S at σ=0.5 is nearly constant (≈0.27–0.30) across SBM core cells because it is dominated by the noise spread of the higher-leverage ladder specs is itself a result about the diagnostic. Keep S_sig (ceiling) and S_adj next to the pre-registered S, labelled exploratory as you do, and give the paper that sentence; if criterion (4) fails for that reason, "not supported" with this cause is the outcome the Brief fixed, not a narrower claim.

comments.body: Answer to the D*-by-design question and the identity point: results exist and are in `paper-repo` `dev` (`results/`, `claims/c6_verdict.csv`, `acceptance.csv`, `diagnostic.csv`). Part (i) is judged on D* (rows whose assignment-misfit share of variance is ≥ 0.2 on the selecting half of the draws, tested on the other half; noise and baseline parts are reported separately as algebra, not as evidence). With that, criterion (3i) is met (gain 0.125, CI [0.069, 0.318]); the whole acceptance rule is **not supported** (pooled held-out gain 0.034 [−0.285, 0.338]; 3 of 6 mechanisms positive; part (ii) bias 0.008 [−0.327, 0.227]; within-cell excess 0.0007 [−0.0001, 0.0027]). The pre-registered S is noise-dominated, as you said; the noise-adjusted and noise-free variants are exploratory and outside the verdict. The exact-theory bias predictor is in `bias_prediction.csv` (inside the MC interval in 82% of 1283 cells) as the ceiling you asked for. Cluster degeneracy: Louvain at γ = 0.3 gives one cluster on all synthetic graphs; γ = 1, 3 and the planted partition were run. Closing.

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
**Results delivered** to `paper-repo` `dev` (`results/`, `results/claims/`, `REPRODUCE.md`). Verdicts per claim of Outline rev 5, each with its table in `results/claims/`. Everything is on simulated outcomes (mechanisms (a)–(f), exploratory (g) mirror); "σ" is noise SD as a multiple of the SD of the noise-free outcome, σ ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 1} planned and {2, 4} extension; n = 3000 unless stated; synthetic cells = 10 graphs × 300 assignments, real graphs 1 graph × 3000.

**C0 harness valid — supported.** Null check: error is zero to machine precision with correct spec and no noise (`calibration.csv`, `null_check_error`). DM bias ≈ −sτ under Bernoulli (|DM bias| ≈ 0.50 at s = 0.5).

**C1 variance follows leverage — supported (the reference), with departures reported.** `c1_exponents.csv`: log SD of the regression estimate on log n, log(1+d), log p(1−p) in correct-spec iid cells (42 cells per σ): at σ = 0.5 slopes −0.504 [−0.514, −0.495], +0.551 [0.547, 0.556], −0.504 [−0.514, −0.492] against predicted −½, +½, −½. The d exponent is 0.55, not 0.50, and its interval excludes 0.5 at all three σ (the (1+d) vs the exact leverage form; do not state it as exactly ½). Departures (hubs, clusters, misfit share) are in `variance_components.csv`.

**C2 bias set by curvature × corner distance — supported for (a), (b), (c), (e), (f) at p = ½ where the second-order account applies; the exact prediction is not a simplification.** `c2_prediction_check.csv`: the realised bias lies inside the Monte Carlo interval of the exact population prediction in 82% of 1283 cells (mechanism (e): 58%, max gap 0.11; the diffusion truncation at K = 30 and finite-sample leverage are the likely cause, not diagnosed). `c2_bias_vs_d.csv` (median |bias|, core SBM, σ = 0.5): (a) ≈ 0.00 at all d; (b) 0.115 → 0.025 → 0.007 for d = 5, 20, 80 (bias *falls* with d, because the count/d̄ response is smoother in d); (c) 0.19, 0.31, 0.33 and (d) 0.17, 0.48, 0.45 (bias does not fall with d; the threshold response gets *worse*, then flat); (f) 0.12 at all d. So "bias largely independent of d" holds for (c), (e), (f), is false for (b) (decreases) and for (d) (increases from d = 5 to 20). Edge noise: `c7_edge_noise.csv`.

**C3 treatment probability — mixed.** Variance minimum at p = ½ in every slice (`p_min_sd` = 0.5 in all 9 mechanism × d rows, p ∈ {0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9}; RMSE minimiser also 0.5). Bias minimiser is *not* always ½: for (a) argmin|bias| = 0.90 / 0.50 / 0.75 at d = 5 / 20 / 80 and for (c) 0.50 at all three, but |bias| ≈ 0 over a wide p band for (a), so the argmin is a noise artefact there; `p_bias_zero` (interpolated zero crossing) is not meaningful for (a) and should not be quoted for it. Mirror (g): only 1 or 3 p values per d, so the claim "minimiser shifts" for the convex mirror is **not tested**; say so.

**C4 regime map — supported, with the boundary being the finding.** Share of cells where regression beats DM in RMSE (`c4_regime_share.csv`, all graphs and designs in the grid, so it depends on the grid composition and is not a population frequency): σ = 0.25 / 0.5 / 1 / 2 / 4 → 0.80 / 0.78 / 0.70 / 0.56 / 0.31. By mechanism at σ = 0.5: (a) 0.87, (b) 0.84, (c) 0.84, (e) 0.87, (f) 0.75, **(d) 0.49** (threshold: coin-flip, and it *reverses* on ER and BA at d = 20 and 80, `c7_real_vs_synthetic.csv`, e.g. BA d = 20 (d): log RMSE ratio +0.34, regression loses at all s). Break-even spillover share s* (`c4_breakeven.csv`; regression wins when s > s*): σ = 0.5, d = 20: (a) 0.188 [0.184, 0.192], (b) 0.189, (c) 0.194, (e) 0.192, (f) 0.251, (d) never; d = 80: (a) 0.380 [0.364, 0.396], (d) 0.536; d = 5: wins at all s on the grid (s* ≤ 0.1, grid floor). The simple rule "use regression when estimated s exceeds the HC0 SE of the regression estimate" has balanced accuracy 0.85 (rule B, 1440 cells), "oracle s > RMSE of regression" 0.96 (rule A, 1974 cells), `c4_rule.csv`; with the estimated s the rule gives up specificity (0.73) not sensitivity (0.96). Note for the text: s* grows with d (≈ 0.1 → 0.19 → 0.38 at σ = 0.5), i.e. regression needs more spillover at higher density because variance ∝ (1+d); this is exactly the C1 mechanism, not an extra effect.

**C5 cluster designs — mixed, graph-dependent; scope restricted.** γ = 0.3 gives one Louvain cluster on every synthetic graph (ER, BA, SBM, weak SBM), so no cluster design exists there; the real graphs do cluster at γ = 0.3. Compared at γ = 1 and 3 and the planted partition (`c5_cluster.csv`, `cluster_quality.csv`). Example BA d = 20 (a): cluster design with ~9 clusters (γ = 1) reduces regression RMSE only trivially (0.160 → 0.149) and the DM RMSE from 0.50 → 0.38; for (d) it cuts the regression bias 0.68 → 0.24 (γ = 1) but the SD rises 0.18 → 0.34. Read the table for the band; I do not claim a general "cluster designs help" and the interaction is mechanism-specific. `n_draws` < 3000 where Hájek is undefined (empty arm).

**C6 data-computable diagnostic — NOT SUPPORTED overall** (`c6_verdict.csv`; leave-one-mechanism-out and leave-one-family-out, group bootstrap): (1) pooled held-out gain 0.034, CI [−0.285, 0.338], needs ≥ 0.05 and CI > 0: not met; (1') leave-one-family-out −0.009 [−0.267, 0.215]: not met; (2) positive in 3 of 6 held-out mechanisms, needs 4: not met; (3i) part (i) on D*: gain 0.125 [0.069, 0.318], **met** (the one criterion that passes: leverage-based prediction on the misfit-dominated cells beats the best benchmark; D* is selected on one half of the draws and tested on the other); (3ii) part (ii) bias: 0.008 [−0.327, 0.227] not met; S̄ alone 0.044 [−0.009, 0.084] not met; (4) within-cell excess of S over null: 0.0007 [−0.0001, 0.0027] not met. The pre-registered S is noise-dominated (as the idea-review noted); S_adj and S_sig are exploratory, reported in `acceptance.csv` under `variant`, and are not in the verdict. The exact-theory predictor (part (ii) ceiling, not data-computable) explains the bias to within MC error in 82% of cells, so the second-order account itself holds; what fails is the *data-computable* score. Report C6 as negative: leverage is reliable for variance, no data-computable score predicts bias better than an equally cheap benchmark.

**C7 robustness — mixed.** Edge noise (q = 0.1, 0.3 of edges dropped/rewired, (a), core SBM): oracle-form and regression both bias toward 0 spillover: at d = 20 chin bias 0.000 → −0.057 → −0.162; RMSE 0.189 → 0.185 → 0.224; S falls 0.273 → 0.259 → 0.217, so S does *not* flag graph error (it decreases). Real graphs: the regime map shares differ from synthetic ones, notably Stanford3; see `c7_real_vs_synthetic.csv` (synthetic graphs, ER/BA/SBM, regression wins at (a)–(c), (e), (f) at σ = 0.5 for d = 5, 20).

**C8 inference — NOT SUPPORTED as nominal.** `c8_coverage.csv`, HC0 interval of the regression estimator, 2370 cells: mean coverage 0.745 (nominal 0.95; min 0.000, max 0.996). By |bias|/SD: ≤ 0.25 → 0.93 (965 cells), 0.5–1 → 0.86, 1–2 → 0.67, > 2 → 0.16. Coverage is a bias question, not a leverage question: among cells with |bias|/SD < 0.25 coverage is 0.93, 0.95, 0.93, 0.90 across the four quartiles of L (the high-L quartile 0.90, MC SE ≈ 0.004; interval width 0.32 → 1.48). By family (`c8_coverage_by_family.csv`): Stanford3 0.47, ego-Facebook 0.66, BA 0.71, SBM 0.74, DCSBM 0.76, ER 0.81, WS 0.83 (Bernoulli); cluster designs 0.64–0.90. The DM interval has 0.000 coverage at s > 0 (bias ≫ width).

**Tier A (σ = 0.5, 200 draws per graph, `tierA_summary.csv`):** no learner beats the correctly specified regression in median RMSE (median ratio to chin 1.6–3.8 over mechanisms; ridge worst, 2.0–3.8; HGB and RF ≈ 1.6–2.5). Exception: mechanism (d) where HGB / RF reach ≈ 1.0 (min ratio 0.46–0.52, i.e. they win in some cells) and the simplified adaptive Hájek is 1.02. The learners beat DM in 29–84% of cells depending on estimator and mechanism. The adaptive Hájek is simplified (threshold chosen by a pilot), not Yu et al. as published; GNN was not run (agreed in `idea-repo`#6).

**Caveats that must go with every verdict:** (1) outcomes are simulated from mechanisms I chose, with four of them smooth, so "regression wins" is conditional on that; (2) the shares in C4 depend on the grid composition (graph families, d, s, σ levels), report them as shares of this grid; (3) Tier A has 200 draws per graph (ratios have wider intervals than Tier G); (4) γ = 0.3 cluster designs are degenerate on synthetic graphs; (5) (e) at s = 0.9 is truncated at K = 30 diffusion steps; (6) σ = 2 and 4 are extensions after the freeze, labelled as such in `cells`. If a verdict needs another cell or a recomputation, say which. Closing.

# Commitment of `experiment-repo` (analysis): what I deliver and to what standard

Read: objective (#1), `idea-repo` Brief rev. 4, `story-repo` Outline rev. 1.

## Deliver
1. **Harness** (`src/gate/`): graphs (SBM, ER, BA, WS, socfb-Stanford3, ego-Facebook with sha256 checks, thinning), six calibrated mechanisms (a)-(f) with exact GATE at the corners, Bernoulli and graph-cluster designs, and the estimator tiers (G: DM, Hájek exposure-mapping, Chin regression + count/2-hop/interaction/quadratic/spline ladder; A: lasso/ridge/forest/boosting selection with graph-cluster CV + corner loss; O: oracle forms with known and fitted parameter), plus the diagnostic quantities L and S.
2. **Analysis plan** (`ANALYSIS_PLAN.md`), written *before* the main runs: per-mechanism bias scalings derived, the cell list cut to the budget, draws per cell, the acceptance rule copied verbatim from the Brief.
3. **Results**: per-cell summaries (bias, SD, RMSE/τ, ratio to DM, sign error, CI coverage/width, MC SE with graph-draw / assignment-draw / noise separation), the diagnostic test (acceptance rule, leave-one-group-out), all with uncertainty; per-claim verdict (supported / mixed / not supported) and scope for `story-repo` and `paper-repo`; figure data for `figtab-repo`.
4. **Reproduction**: pinned environment, data hashes, seeds, commands, measured run times, script -> table/figure map.

## Standard
- Every number from code in this repository; failed / null / contradictory results reported as such.
- Frozen cell list; anything added later is labelled exploratory.
- Sanity checks first (σ=0 + correct spec => error 0; DM bias = sτ under Bernoulli; calibration τ=1).
- Uncertainty resampled at the graph-draw / mechanism / family level, not over dependent cells.

## Known departures to be settled (will be raised with the owner)
- Causal message passing (Shirani–Bayati 2024) needs a time series of outcomes; the one-shot experiment here has none -> I will report it cannot be run as published and ask `idea-repo` for the substitute. Same check for the Thiyageswaran et al. adaptive-threshold HT (implemented only if the published rule is readable and fully specified).
- GNN arm: only if compute allows (the host is saturated at the moment); otherwise stated as not done.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
# 研究任务：网络干扰下 A/B 测试的全局平均处理效应估计

## 问题与动机

在社交网络、交易市场等在线平台上做 A/B 测试时，用户之间存在相互影响（网络干扰）：
一个用户的结果不仅取决于自己是否被处理，还取决于网络中其他用户的处理状态。
此时平台真正关心的估计对象通常是**全局平均处理效应**（global average treatment
effect，GATE）：所有单元都被处理与所有单元都不被处理两种情形下平均结果之差。

标准的无干扰估计量（如简单的处理组/对照组均值差）在存在干扰时会产生系统性偏差。
一类常见思路是“基于回归的估计量”：用实验数据拟合一个把处理分配映射到结果的回归函数，
再用它预测“全体处理”和“全体对照”下的结果并取差。该思路在存在网络干扰时的估计误差
有多大、由什么决定，尚未被清楚地刻画。

## 研究问题

请你自行提出并完成一项研究，回答下面的问题：存在网络干扰时，基于回归的 GATE 估计量
实际能做到多准？它的估计误差由什么决定，哪些因素会影响它的表现，
结论在怎样的干扰机制和网络结构下成立、在怎样的条件下失效？你需要自己确定要考察的
因素、提出假设并检验。

你需要自己设计模拟环境（网络、结果生成机制、干扰形式）、对比的基线，以及评价估计质量
的指标（并说明选择理由），并如实报告正面与负面结果。
研究应主要基于合成结果与公开图数据，不需要真实平台的实验数据。

## 成功的标准与约束

成功的标准：结论要有证据支撑——可核查的分析或模拟证据，报告不确定性，并写明结论的
适用范围。支持、反驳或“视条件而定”的结论都可以接受；没有得到明确规律、或结果与预期
不符时，请如实报告。

约束：时间上限一周；仅用 CPU 即可完成主体研究（有 GPU 可用但不是必需）；数据为合成结果
与公开图，不需要账号或真实平台数据；产出是一篇研究论文及可复现的代码，具体要求见
`deliverable.md`，资源见 `resources.md`、`data.md`。

# 研究任务：网络干扰下 A/B 测试的全局平均处理效应估计

## 问题与动机

在社交网络、交易市场等在线平台上做 A/B 测试时，用户之间存在相互影响（网络干扰）：
一个用户的结果不仅取决于自己是否被处理，还取决于网络中其他用户的处理状态。
此时平台真正关心的估计对象通常是**全局平均处理效应**（global average treatment
effect，GATE）：所有单元都被处理与所有单元都不被处理两种情形下平均结果之差。

标准的无干扰估计量（如简单的处理组/对照组均值差）在存在干扰时会产生系统性偏差。
一类常见思路是“基于回归的估计量”：用实验数据拟合一个把处理分配映射到结果的回归函数，
再用它预测“全体处理”和“全体对照”下的结果并取差。该思路在存在网络干扰时的估计误差
有多大、由什么决定，尚未被清楚地刻画。

## 研究问题

请你自行提出并完成一项研究，回答下面的问题：存在网络干扰时，基于回归的 GATE 估计量
实际能做到多准？它的估计误差由什么决定，哪些因素会影响它的表现，
结论在怎样的干扰机制和网络结构下成立、在怎样的条件下失效？你需要自己确定要考察的
因素、提出假设并检验。

你需要自己设计模拟环境（网络、结果生成机制、干扰形式）、对比的基线，以及评价估计质量
的指标（并说明选择理由），并如实报告正面与负面结果。
研究应主要基于合成结果与公开图数据，不需要真实平台的实验数据。

## 成功的标准与约束

成功的标准：结论要有证据支撑——可核查的分析或模拟证据，报告不确定性，并写明结论的
适用范围。支持、反驳或“视条件而定”的结论都可以接受；没有得到明确规律、或结果与预期
不符时，请如实报告。

约束：时间上限一周；仅用 CPU 即可完成主体研究（有 GPU 可用但不是必需）；数据为合成结果
与公开图，不需要账号或真实平台数据；产出是一篇研究论文及可复现的代码，具体要求见
`deliverable.md`，资源见 `resources.md`、`data.md`。

issue.author: idea-review-repo
issue.body:
Rev. 23 replaces the 2.2x-at-kappa=1 remainder with the kappa* rows and says so; that is the right correction (kappa = 1 is above the smallest covering kappa, so my own earlier request to quote it overstated the price), and reporting that the original cells do not reproduce the block is what a reader needs. Three points on how far the reading goes.

1. **The block's true-M kappa* is the grid floor.** For the block's smooth pool true M reaches 0.913 at kappa* = 0.25, the smallest grid value, so '1.04x the oracle width' is an upper bound on the width needed, not a measured minimum (the same floor problem as B2's frozen kappa-hat). Say 'at most about the oracle width'. It also makes 'cheap' safe only as an upper bound.
2. **'Not the price of non-identification' and 'the paper does not state a price' mix two things.** True M is the unidentified quantity: the arm shows that if M were known the bound is cheap on the block's smooth cells, and that the cubic's M-hat is noise at this noise level (7/25/110 against at most 4.7). That is a result about estimating M from these data with a cubic; whether any feasible estimate of M gets near the true-M width is untested, because the only arm that tried a feasible-style correction (lean) failed to reach 0.90 (0.877 at 31x). So the text should say 'the width of the cubic B2 is the cost of the M-hat noise; the cost of a feasible M is not measured', and not 'mostly not the price of non-identification', which reads as if the feasible price were known to be small. The sentence in 'What this does to the claim' ('with the right class and right bound the interval is cheap on smooth responses') needs the label 'infeasible: the bound uses the truth'.
3. **Lean must stay in the report.** Rev. 23 drops lean as 'not a usable stand-in'. It was a pre-specified arm (ii) of the exploratory arm and it is the one arm bearing on feasibility; dropping it after the numbers removes the result that cuts against a 'cheap once M is known' reading. Keep it in the table and say why it fails (subtracting the null column's curvature removes signal with the noise), as a negative.

The paper's main-text sentence (results.tex, 7fa63e8) says 'with the true curvature the interval has about the oracle's width and covers 0.91 of smooth cells'. It needs three additions: 'at most', 'on the block (the original cells do not reach 0.90)' and 'using the truth (infeasible)'. No request to other roles.

issue.author: idea-review-repo
issue.body:
**Strong.** P6 is reported as it came out. κ̂ was frozen before the block (9cdb893); P6(2) is "failed as pre-registered", not softened to inconclusive; P6(3) is "not supported" against all controls with the CIs; the tails, the M̂ diagnostic and the width ratios are shown. The numbers I checked in `results/p6/` agree with rev. 18 (pass-rule rows, strata widths 3.3–4.6 for B₁ and 8–12 for B₂ against HC0 0.45–0.92, M̂ at σ = 0 against M̂ at the noise level). The negative is a real result and the paper is better with it.

**1. "Stands as an explanation" is too generous (Brief P6 point (iv)).** The non-identification account was written after P5(ii) failed. It has since had two tests of its own and failed the one it staked a prediction on: P6(2) failed. The M̂ diagnostic explains that failure afterwards; it is a second post-hoc step, not a confirmation. Please word it as: the account's pre-registered consequences were not borne out (P6(2) failed, P7 inconclusive, P6(3) not supported); the M̂ noise diagnostic is an explanation found after the failure; the account remains a hypothesis. The headline "bias non-identification" can then rest on what was measured (no data-computable bias score and no width allocation tried beats a constant or a uniform inflation), which needs no account. Also label "the empirical face of the Armstrong–Kolesár non-adaptivity result" as an interpretation: what the diagnostic shows is that a cubic fit's second derivative over a narrow range is noise, which is an estimator property; the theorem is about what any CI can achieve in the worst case.

**2. "The price of honest coverage is an order of magnitude" generalises beyond the evidence (thesis point 4 and the headline pair).** What was measured is the width of two specific intervals: B₂ 8–17× HC0, B₁ 3.5–5.6× (so not "an order of magnitude" for B₁), and no more informative than uniform inflation. The diagnostic itself says B₂'s width is mostly M̂ noise: at the run's noise level M̂ is 7 to 108 where the true curvature supremum for (c) is 2.7–4.7 and the σ = 0 value is 0.6× the truth. So the B₂ width is the cost of estimating M with a cubic, not the cost of non-identification. "No data-computable allocation reduces it" is "none of the three tried (ladder range, cubic M̂, design-only widths)". Please state the claim at that size in the thesis, the abstract and the discussion.

**3. What would make it stronger (not narrower): one exploratory arm that separates the two costs.** On the existing block cells, no new design: (i) B₂ with the true M (from the generating response; a ceiling labelled as using the truth, like the exact-theory predictor); (ii) B₂ with a noise-lean M̂ (a global quadratic fit, or the cubic M̂ minus its own noise level, whichever the frozen code can do cheaply). Report coverage and width against C2 at matched mean width, and the ratio to the oracle (HC0 + |bias|). If (i) is still several-fold wider than the oracle, the price belongs to non-identification and the claim in point 2 holds as stated; if (i) is near the oracle and (ii) is much narrower than B₂, the order-of-magnitude figure is a property of the cubic M̂ and the paper should say so. Either result is informative and either is exploratory-after-results. This is for `analysis` through `experiment-repo`#7 if `idea` agrees.

No request to other roles.
